subject: RE: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU data residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Müller <l.muller@nordbank.de>
Cc: Anja Schmidt <a.schmidt@nordbank.de>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU data residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Lukas / Anja,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — appreciate you walking through NordBank's latency and regulatory constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep the momentum: 

Recap from our call:
- Primary requirement: All customer data (inference requests and related logs) must remain and be processed within the EU.
- Secondary: Cross-region failover is acceptable only to another EU region; cross-border routing to non-EU regions is not permitted.
- Performance target: sub-150ms p50 inference for 512-token requests for customer-facing flows.
- Interest area: understanding tradeoffs between Hosted (Redwood API in EU), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in EU), and Private (VPC / on-prem).

What we can offer today:
- Hosted API (EU): We run hosted endpoints in eu-central-1 and eu-west-1. Data and logs are stored in-region; we can configure routing to pin traffic to a single EU region. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and our standard usage SLA (see attached SLA).
- Dedicated (EU): Reserved capacity hosted in your own dedicated GPU pool within an EU region. Provides predictable throughput and stricter isolation (single-tenant pools). We can center capacity in a chosen region and restrict cross-region failover to EU-only.
- Private VPC / On-prem: For the strictest compliance profile, we deploy a private control plane and customer-managed compute (VPC or on-prem appliance). Data never leaves your network unless you enable a specific integration. This is the longer lead option but satisfies most audit/sovereignty requirements.

Open items / proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether EU-only processing means a single region (e.g., eu-central-1) or any EU region is acceptable for failover?
2) If single-region is required, can you share expected qps and peak concurrency so we can size Dedicated or Private proposals?
3) We'd like to schedule a 30-min deep-dive with our deployment architect (Aditya Rao) to walk through network, KMS, and validation for Private/VPC options. Suggested times: Mon/Tue next week, 09:00–12:00 CET.

Attachments: Redwood-SLA.pdf, deployment-options-one-pager.pdf (short one-pager that highlights tradeoffs and lead times).

If you prefer, we can start with Hosted pinned to eu-central-1 to prove performance and then move to Dedicated/Private for contractual/regulatory controls — that’s a common path.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

---
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform.

From: Lukas Müller <l.muller@nordbank.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anja Schmidt <a.schmidt@nordbank.de>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU data residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications: 

1) EU-only: We need data processing to remain within the EU. Failover is acceptable but only to another EU region — ideally eu-central-1 as our preference. Single-region is preferred for now due to audit controls, but we can accept automated failover to eu-west-1 in a DR scenario.
2) Traffic profile: Production target is ~120 qps sustained with ~800 peak qps for short bursts. Typical request sizes average ~350 tokens.
3) KMS: We require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for encryption at rest.

Two follow-ups: 
- Can Hosted pinned to eu-central-1 support customer-managed KMS? If not, do Dedicated or Private support it out-of-the-box?
- What are lead times and estimated monthly costs for Dedicated vs Private for the traffic profile above? If you can provide a ballpark (order-of-magnitude) we can decide which path to pursue.

Appreciate scheduling the deep-dive — Tue morning CET works for us.

Cheers,
Lukas
Senior Product Manager | NordBank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Müller <l.muller@nordbank.de>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Anja Schmidt <a.schmidt@nordbank.de>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 12:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU data residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Lukas / Anja — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Answering each point below plus next steps: 

KMS & Hosted:
- Hosted API in the EU currently supports provider-managed keys by default. We can support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Hosted in eu-central-1, but it requires a brief security review and an entitlement — this is routinely done and we have a standard onboarding checklist.

Dedicated:
- Dedicated pools provide stronger isolation and can be configured to use customer-managed KMS keys (we integrate with AWS KMS and most major providers). Lead time: typically 4–6 weeks to provision and validate in a single EU region, depending on capacity and contract.
- For your profile (120 sustained / 800 burst; avg 350 tokens) a small Dedicated pool (4x A10G-equivalent nodes with autoscale headroom) is a likely starting point. Ballpark monthly: €18k–€30k depending on commit level and quantization profile. We'll do a more accurate sizing after the deep-dive.

Private VPC / On-prem:
- This option provides the strictest controls — full VPC deployment, private control plane, and on-prem/offline packaging if required. Lead time: typically 8–12 weeks (longer if on-prem hardware procurement is needed). Setup includes network validation, KMS integration (customer keys), and acceptance testing.
- Costs: typically higher for on-prem due to hardware + support; VPC deployments are comparable to Dedicated plus a platform licensing fee. We'll put exact numbers in a proposal.

Hosted pinning & failover: 
- We can pin traffic to eu-central-1 for both Hosted and Dedicated. For Hosted, automated cross-region failover can be restricted to EU-only regions; we can also disable cross-region failover if you prefer manual failover for audit reasons.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Deep-dive with Aditya (deployment architect) to validate network topology, expected metrics, and KMS flow — Tue 08:30–09:00 CET or Tue 10:00–10:30 CET? Please confirm a slot.
2) We'll run a short security onboarding checklist for BYOK (I'll share the form).
3) I'll assemble a ballpark Dedicated vs Hosted cost worksheet after the call and follow up with a formal SOW if you want Dedicated/Private sizing.

If you’d like to pilot faster, starting with Hosted pinned to eu-central-1 (with BYOK enabled) gives the fastest path to validate performance. If procurement requires Reserved capacity up-front, Dedicated is the next step.

Thanks — looping in Aditya for the scheduling.

Best,
Marissa

---
Aditya — can you pick a 30-min slot tomorrow morning to join? I included the network/KMS checklist in the shared doc (link below).
